FOREWORD This Indian standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Marine Engineering and Safety Aids Sectional Committee had been approved by Transport Engineering Division Council. Steering gear provides mechanism for effecting movement of the rudder for the purpose of steering the vessel. Since steering gear is of critical application in any sea going vessel it is required to be of sound construction, fault free operation and has to have inbuih safeguards. This standard has been devided in six sections: Section Section Section Section Section Section 1 2 3 4 5 6 General Performance Construction and design Steering control systems Electric power circuits, electric control circuits, monitoring and alarms Testing and trials

The composition of the Committee responsible for formulation of this standard is given in Annex A. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant placed retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

SHIPBUILDING -- HYDRAULIC STEERING GEARS FOR VESSELS BELOW 500 GRT -- GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
1 SCOPE

3.5 Power Actuating System The hydraulic equipment provided for supplying power to turn the rudder stock, comprising a steering gear power unit or units, together with associated pipes and fittings, and a rudder actuator. The power actuating systems may share common mechanical components, for example, tiller quadrant and rudder stock, or components serving the same purpose. 3.6 Rudder Actuator The component which converts directly hydraulic pressure into mechanical action to move the rudder. 3.7 Steering Gear Control Systems The equipment by which orders are transmitted from the navigating bridge to the steering gear power units. Steering gear control systems comprise transmitters, receivers, hydraulic control pumps and their associated motors, motor controllers, piping and cables. 3.8 Steering Gear Power Unit in the case of electro-hydraulic steering gear, an electric motor and its associated electrical equipment and connected pump; and b) in the case of other hydraulic steering gear, a driving engine and connected pump. 4 INSTALLATION The steering gear shall be secured to the seating by bolts and suitable chocking arrangements shall be provided. The seating shall be of substantial construction. 5 MATERIALS 5.1 All the steering gear components and the rudder stock shall be of sound and reliable construction. 5.2 All components transmitting mechanical forces to the rudder stock shall be manufactured and tested accordhg to the relevant requirements of applicable Indian Standards. 5.3 Ram cylinders; hydraulic power piping; flanges and fittings; and all steering gear components transmitting mechanical forces to the rudder stock (such as tillers, quadrants, or similar components) 1 a)

This standard specifies requirements pertaining to design and construction of steering gear for sea-going vessels below 500 grt. 2 REFERENCE The following standard contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provision of this standard. At the time of publication, the edition indicated was valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent edition of the standard indicated below: IS No. 2825:1969 Title Code for unfired pressure vessels
SECTION 3 DEFINITIONS 1 GENERAL

For the purpose of this standard following definitions shall apply.
3.1 Auxiliary Steering Gear

The equipment other than any part of the main steering gear necessary to steer the ship in the event of failure of the main steering gear but not including the tiller, quadrant or components serving the same purpose. 3.2 Main Steering Gear The machinery rudder actuator(s), the steering gear power units, if any, and ancillary equipment and the means of applying torque to the rudder stock (for example, tiller or quadrant) necessary for effecting movement of the rudder for the purpose of steering the ship under normal service conditions.
3.3 Maximum Ahead Service Speed

The greatest speed which the ship is designed to maintain in service at sea at its deepest seagoing draught. 3.4 Maximum Working Pressure The expected pressure in the system when steering gear is operated to comply with 7.2 (b).

IS 15053:2001 shall be of steel or other equivalent ductile material. In general, such material shall not to have an elongation of less than 12 per cent nor a tensile strength in excess of 600 N/mm*. The use of ductile (nodular) iron castings shall be acceptable for pressure housing of rotary vane type actuators and valves. 6 RUDDER, RUDDER STOCK, TILLER AND QUADRANT Rudder, rudder stock, tiller and quadrant shall be designed in accordance with the requirements of applicable Rules of the Classification Societies.

in a cargo ship, the main steering gear is capable of operating the rudder as required by 7.2 (b) while operating with all power units; and b) the main steering gear is arranged so that after a single failure in its piping system or in one of the power units the defect can be isolated so that steering capability is regained. 7.5 Main and auxiliary steering gear power units shall be: a) b) arranged tore-start automatically when power is restored after a power failure; capable of being brought into operation from a position on the navigating bridge. In the event of a power failure to the steering gear power units, an audible and visual alarm shall be given on the navigating bridge; and arranged so that transfer between units can be readiiy effected.

a)

7 GENERAL 7.1 Unless the main steering gear comprises two or more identical power units, every ship shall be provided with a main steering gear and an auxiliary steering gear. The main steering gear and the auxiliary steering gear shall be so arranged that the failure of one of them shall not render the other one inoperative. 7.2 The main steering gear and rudder stock shall be: Of adequate strength and capable of steering the ship at maximum ahead speed; b) Capable of putting the rudder over from 35� on one side to 35� on the other side with the ship at its deepest seagoing draught and running ahead at maximum ahead service speed and under the same conditions, from 35� on either side to 30� on the other side in not more than 28 seconds; c) Operated by power where necessary to meet the requirements of (b) and in any case when rudder stock over 120 mm diameter in way of the tiller is provided; and d) So designed that they shall not be damaged at maximum astern speed. a) 7.3 The auxiliary steering gear shall be: a) Of adequate strength and capable of steering the ship at navigable speed and of being brought speedily into action in an emergency; b) Capable of putting the rudder over from 15� on one side to 15� on the other side in not more than 60 seconds with the ship at its deepest seagoing draft and running ahead service speed or 7 knots, whichever is the greate~ and c) Operated by power where necessary to meet . . the requirements of (b) and in any case when rudder stock over 230 mm diameter in way of the tiller is provided. 7.4 Where the main steering gear comprises two or more identical power units, an auxiliary steering gear need not be fitted, provided that:

c)

7.6 A means of communication shall be provided between the navigating bridge and the steering gear compartment. 7.7 Manually operated gears shall only be acceptable when the operation does not require an effort exceeding 160 N under normal conditions. 8 RUDDER ANGLE LIMITERS Power-operated steering gears shall be provided with positive arrangements, such as limit switches, for stopping the gear before the rudder stops are reached. These arrangements shall be synchronized with the gear itself and not with the steering gear control.
SECTION 3 CONSTRUCTION 9 GENERAL AND DESIGN

9.1 Rudder actuators shall be designed in accordance with the relevant requirement of IS 2825 with joint being designed for 100 percent efficiency factor. 9.2 Accumulators, if fitted, shall comply with the requirements of 9.1. 9.3 All welded joints within the pressure boundary of a rudder actuator or connecting parts transmitting mechanical loads shall be full penetration type or of equivalent strength. 9.4 The construction shall be such as to minimize local concentration of stress. 9.5 The design pressure for calculation to determine the scantlings of piping and other steering gear components subjected to internal hydraulic pressure shall be at least 1.25 times the maximum working pressure to be expected under the operational conditions specified in 7.2(b) taking into account any 2

Arrangements for bleeding air from the hydraulic system shall be provided, where necessary. 11.2 Relief valves shall be fitted to any part of the hydraulic system which can be isolated and in which pressure can be generated from the power source or from external forces. The setting of the relief valves shall not exceed the design pressure. The valves shall be of adequate size and so arranged as to avoid an undue rise in pressure above the design pressure.
11.3 Relief valves, for protecting any part of the hydraulic system which can be isolated, required by 11.2 shall comply with the following:

10 COMPONENTS 10.1 All steering gear components transmitting mechanical forces to the rudder stock, which are not protected against overload by structural rudder stops or mechanical buffers, shall have a strength at least equivalent to that of the rudder stock in way of the tiller.

a) The setting pressure shall not to be less than 1.25 times the maximum working pressure; and b) The minimum discharge capacity of the relief valve(s) shall not to be less than 110 percent of the total capacity of the pump which can be delivered through it (them). Under such conditions the rise in pressure shall not exceed 10 per cent of the setting pressure. In this regard, due consideration shall be given to extreme foreseen ambient conditions in respect of oil viscosity.
12 FLEXIBLE HOSES

10.2 Oil seals between non-moving parts, forming part of the external pressure boundary, shall be of the metal type or of an equivalent type. 10.3 Oil seals between moving parts, forming part of the external pressure boundary, shall be duplicated, so that the failure of one seal does not render the actuator inoperative. Alternative arrangements providing equivalent protection against leakage may be accepted. 10.4 Hydraulic power operated steering gears shall be provided with the: a) arrangements to maintain the cleanliness of the hydraulic fluid taking into consideration the type and design of the hydraulic system; and a fixed storage tank having sufficient capacity to recharge at least one po wer actuating system including the reservoir, where the main steering gear is required to b power operated. The storage tank shall be pemmnently connected by piping in such a manner that the hydraulic systems can be readily recharged from a position within the steering gear compartment and provided with a contents gauge.
AND RELIEF VALVE ARRANGE-

12.1 Hose assemblies may be installed between two points where flexibility is required but are not subjected to torsional deflection (twisting) under normal operating conditions. In general, the hose shall be limited to the length necessary to provide for flexibility and for proper operation of machinery. 12.2 Hoses shall be high pressure hydraulic hoses according to recognized standards and suitable for the fluids, pressures, temperatures and ambient conditions in question.

12.3 Burst pressure of hoses shall not be less than four times the design pressure.

13.2 Any main and auxiliary steering gear control system operable from the navigating bridge shall comply with the following: a) Means shall be provided in the steering gear compartment for disconnecting any control system operable from the navigating bridge from the steering gear it serves; and b) The system shall be capable of being brought into operation from a position on the navigating bridge. 13.3 The angular position of the rudder shall: a) be indicated on the navigating bridge if the main steering gear is power operated. The rudder angle indication shall be independent of the steering gear control system; and be recognizable in the steering gear compartment.

15.1 Electric control systems shall be independent and separated as far as practicable throughout their length.

b)

15.2 Each main and auxiliary electric control system which is operable from the navigating bridge shall comply with the following: a) It shall be served with electric power by a separate circuit supplied from the associated steering gear power circuit from a point within the steering gear compartment, or directly from the same section of the switchboard busbars, main or emergency, to which the associated steering gear power circuit is connected; and b) Each separate circuit shall be provided with short circuit protection only. 16 MONITORING AND ALARMS 16.1 All alarms associated with steering gear faults shall be indicated on the navigating bridge. The alarms shall be both audible and visual. Mandatory list of steering alarms is given below: Steering Alarms, Display and Indication Equipment/ Characteristic

diagram showing the change-over procedures for steering gear control systems and steering gear actuating systems shall be permanently displayed in the wheelhouse and in the steering gear compartment.

in the case of polyphase circuits, an alarm to indicate single phasing shall be provided for each main and auxiliary motor circuit. Protective devices shall operate at not less than twice the full load current of the motor or circuit protected and shall allow excess current to pass during the normal accelerating period of the motors. 14.2 Indicators for running indication of each main and auxiliary motor shall be installed on the navigating bridge and at a suitable main machinery control position. 14.3 Each electric or electro-hydraulic steering gear comprising one or more power units shall be served by at least two exclusive circuits fed directly from the main switchboard; however one of the circuits maybe supplied through the emergency switchboard. An auxiliary electric or electro-hydraulic steering gear may be connected to one of the circuits supplying the main steering gear. Is 15053:2001 SECTION 6 TESTING 17 TESTING 17.1 After installation on board the vessel the steering AND TRIALS

the standard have been met. The trial shall include the operation of the following: a) The steering ger, including demonstration of the performance required by 7.2 (b) and 7.3 (b). If the vessel cannot be tested at the deepest draught, alternative trial conditions may be specially considered; b) The steering gear power units, including transfer between steering gear power units; c) The isolation of one power actuating system, checking the time for regaining steering capability; d) The hydraulic fluid recharging systems; e) The steering gear controls, including transfer of control and local controls; The means of communication between the f) steering gear compartment and wheelhouses, also the engine room, it applicable; and g) The alarms and indicators.

gear shall be subjected to the required hydrostatic and running tests. 17.2 Each type of power unit pump shall be subjected to a type test. The type test shall be for a duration of not less than 100 hours. The test arrangements shall be such that the pump may run in idling conditions, and at maximum delivery capacity at maximum working pressure. During the test, idling periods shall be alternated with periods at maximum delivery capacity at maximum working pressure. The passage from one condition to another shall occur at least as quickly as on board. During the whole test no abnormal heating, excessive vibration or other irregularities are permitted. After the test, the pump shall be opened out and inspected. 18 TRIALS
